source_text: Age jam, qui voles curiositatem melius exercere in negotio salutis tuae, percurre Ecclesias apostolicas, apud quas ipsae adhuc cathedrae Apostolorum suis locis praesident; apud quas ipsae authenticae litterae eorum recitantur, sonantes vocem et repraesentantes faciem uniuscujusque. Proxima est tibi Achaia? habes Corinthum. Si non longe es a Macedonia, habes Philippos, habes Thessalonicenses. Si potes in Asiam tendere, habes Ephesum. Si autem Italiae adjaces, habes Romam, unde nobis quoque auctoritas praesto est. Ista quam felix Ecclesia! cui totam doctrinam Apostoli cum sanguine suo profuderunt; ubi Petrus passioni Dominicae adaequatur; ubi Paulus Joannis exitu coronatur; ubi Apostolus Joannes, posteaquam, in oleum igneum demersus, nihil passus est, in insulam relegatur; videamus quid didicerit, quid docuerit, cum Africanis quoque Ecclesiis contesserarit. Unum Deum novit, creatorem universitatis, et Christum Jesum ex virgine Maria Filium Dei creatoris, et carnis resurrectionem; Legem et Prophetas cum evangelicis et apostolicis litteris miscet, et inde potat fidem; eam aqua signat, Sancto Spiritu vestit, eucharistia pascit, ad martyrium exhortatur, et ita adversus hanc institutionem neminem recipit. Haec est institutio, non dico jam quae futuras haereses praenuntiabat, sed de qua haereses prodierunt. Sed non fuerunt ex illa, ex quo factae sunt adversus illam. Etiam de olivae nucleo mitis et optimae et necessariae asper oleaster oritur; etiam de papavere ficus gratissimae et suavissimae ventosa et vana caprificus exsurgit. Ita et haereses de nostro frutice, non nostro genere; veritatis grano, sed mendacio sylvestres.
pass_a_gloss: Now, if you want to exercise curiosity better in the matter of your salvation, run through the apostolic Churches, in which the very chairs of the Apostles still preside in their places; in which their authentic letters are read, sounding the voice and representing the face of each one. Is Achaia near you? you have Corinth. If you are not far from Macedonia, you have Philippi, you have the Thessalonians. If you can stretch into Asia, you have Ephesus. If, however, you are adjacent to Italy, you have Rome, from which also authority is at hand for us. What a happy Church! to which the Apostles poured out all their doctrine with their own blood; where Peter is equal to the Lord's passion; where Paul is crowned with John's departure; where the Apostle John, after having been immersed in fiery oil and having suffered nothing, is relegated to an island; let us see what he learned, what he taught, when he contended with the African Churches as well. He knows one God, the creator of the universe, and Christ Jesus, the Son of God the creator, from the virgin Mary, and the resurrection of the flesh; he mixes the Law and the Prophets with the evangelical and apostolic letters, and from there he drinks faith; he seals it with water, clothes it with the Holy Spirit, feeds it with the Eucharist, exhorts it to martyrdom, and thus against this institution he receives no one. This is the institution, I do not say now which predicted future heresies, but from which heresies have come forth. But they were not from it, since they were made against it. Also from the nucleus of the olive, a wild and bitter oleaster arises; also from the poppy, a fig of the most pleasing and sweetest, a windy and vain caprifig springs up. So also heresies from our fruit, not our kind; from the grain of truth, but wild with falsehood.

pass_b_english: If you want to put your curiosity to better use for your own salvation, then make the rounds of the apostolic churches. In those churches the very chairs of the apostles still preside in their original places, and their authentic letters are read aloud, echoing each apostle's voice and preserving his likeness. Is Achaia nearby? You have Corinth. Not far from Macedonia? You have Philippi and the Thessalonians. Able to reach Asia? You have Ephesus. If you border Italy, you have Rome, from which authority is also close at hand for us. What a blessed church! The apostles poured out their entire teaching there with their own blood; Peter matched the Lord's passion there; Paul was crowned with John's death there; and the apostle John, after being plunged into boiling oil and suffering no harm, was exiled to an island. Let us see what he learned and taught when he contended with the African churches as well. He acknowledges one God, the Creator of all, and Christ Jesus, the Son of God the Creator, born of the Virgin Mary, and the resurrection of the flesh. He blends the Law and the Prophets with the gospel and apostolic writings, draws his faith from them, seals it with water, clothes it with the Holy Spirit, feeds it with the Eucharist, urges it toward martyrdom, and on that basis admits no one who opposes this rule. This is the rule — not merely one that foretold future heresies, but the one from which heresies actually sprang. Yet they did not come from it, because they were formed against it. Even from the kernel of the olive a wild, bitter oleaster springs up; even from the poppy a most pleasing and sweet fig, a windy and empty caprifig, arises. So heresies come from our fruit, not our stock — from the grain of truth, but growing wild with falsehood.
